| | **Friend, above all else, I am and will forever be a parent first.** My three kids are well into their adult years, but I still think about them every minute of every day. As a mother, I _always_ worry about their safety — especially right now. There hasn’t been a **single week** in 2022 without a mass shooting. Our schools, our grocery stores, _even our holiday parades_ are not safe from the gun violence epidemic spreading throughout our country. _Enough is enough._ It’s time to enact common-sense gun laws and condemn the permitless carry bills legislators like my opponent have tried to pass. It’s time to mandate background checks and red flag laws, and it’s time to stop sending wishes for peace without any meaningful course of action. **[If you’re ready to join my fight to enact common-sense gun reform, sign my petition today so we can send D.C. the message: Our communities need action, not empty platitudes.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/50712173/366907885/1715611728?refcode=em_220914_guncontrol_rs2&sourceid=1031507&ms=em_220914_guncontrol_rs2&refcode2=cfaf3f34-7034-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkxMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZmFmM2YzNC03MDM0LWVkMTEtYWU4My0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fpsFKO2reTcFesyG8e9mjiu-FTpD1gGsanxCfFM7PNc=&emci=8ec05bba-4734-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&emdi=cfaf3f34-7034-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&ceid=17998091)** | [SIGN ON »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/50712177/366907887/1715611728?refcode=em_220914_guncontrol_rs2&sourceid=1031507&ms=em_220914_guncontrol_rs2&refcode2=cfaf3f34-7034-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkxMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZmFmM2YzNC03MDM0LWVkMTEtYWU4My0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fpsFKO2reTcFesyG8e9mjiu-FTpD1gGsanxCfFM7PNc=&emci=8ec05bba-4734-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&emdi=cfaf3f34-7034-ed11-ae83-281878b83d8a&ceid=17998091)

Our children — and our communities — deserve leadership who cares more about their safety than their rating from the NRA. As your next congresswoman, I promise I’ll fight like only a mother can to end the vicious cycle of gun violence throughout our country.
Thanks for your support, friend.

clean_body: Our communities need action, not empty platitudes. | = | | Friend, above all else, I am and will forever be a parent first. My three kids are well into their adult years, but I still think about them every minute of every day. As a mother, I always worry about their safety — especially right now. There hasn’t been a single week in 2022 without a mass shooting. Our schools, our grocery stores, even our holiday parades are not safe from the gun violence epidemic spreading throughout our country. Enough is enough. It’s time to enact common-sense gun laws and condemn the permitless carry bills legislators like my opponent have tried to pass. It’s time to mandate background checks and red flag laws, and it’s time to stop sending wishes for peace without any meaningful course of action. | Our children — and our communities — deserve leadership who cares more about their safety than their rating from the NRA. As your next congresswoman, I promise I’ll fight like only a mother can to end the vicious cycle of gun violence throughout our country. Thanks for your support, friend. | Hey, team.

Since becoming Arizona’s Democratic nominee for Secretary of State, we’ve had a lot of new folks join our movement, so I wanted to take a moment to reintroduce myself.

You may know me as the election official who led the charge to prove Arizona’s 2020 elections were safe and secure, the former U.S. Marine Marksmanship Instructor who dismantled the right’s Second Amendment lies, or the candidate running against Oath Keeper and extremist Mark Finchem, but really, my story is simple.

**I’m a father, small-business owner, and concerned citizen for our democracy.**

**[I want to share more on why this race and our democracy are so important to me, but first, I have to ask: Will you join me in my fight to become Arizona’s next Secretary of State and protect our democracy by splitting a donation of $10 right now between me and the Arizona Democratic Party?

In 2020, I had the honor to serve as Maricopa County Recorder, running the nation’s _3rd largest voting precinct._ As County Recorder, my work and the work of my bipartisan team stood up to one of the most extensive election audits we’ve ever seen. I dedicated myself to counting every single vote, even when the numbers began to show I’d lost my own race.

[1]Justice Democrats

Nearly 90% of Congressional races are won by the candidate who spends more
money. It’s a tough reality,
Peter, but it’s what we’re up
against.

We’ve won races with less money, though, like when Alexandria
Ocasio-Cortez beat a high-ranking corporate Democrat back in 2018. But
it’s really hard to do, and that’s one of the reasons AOC’s victory
shocked the political establishment to the core.

AOC’s opponent in 2018 spent at least 5 times more than she did on the
primary election. But AOC won because she was what NY-14 needed, had a
strong campaign, and a strong message. We helped her build that
campaign, Peter.

As we build power and see the impact of the Squad in Congress, we’ve been
able to close the spending gap. Then, more challenges came our way. The
political establishment started spending millions through corporate super
PACs to smear our candidates. Centrist and right-wing groups, big
corporations and Wall Street, Big Oil and Big Tech, all started flooding
money into our races to keep corporate Democrats in office.

We continue to shock the political establishment because of our grassroots
support. We do our best to match the unlimited resources of the political
establishment with donations of $3, $18.21 (our average donation this
year), $27 or more from folks like you. We rely on your support 100%
because we don’t and we won’t take a cent from corporate PACs.

And we use your donations strategically,
Peter. We build campaigns to
win, help our candidates hire staff, set up field organizing operations,
support media strategies, and so much more.

It takes a lot of money to win our primaries and transform the Democratic
Party, especially when our opponents are bankrolled by Wall Street and the
Democratic establishment.

One evening earlier this summer, while the Senate was voting on a veterans' health care bill, Raphael Warnock was nowhere to be found.

_**That's just shameful.**_

During his trip to the Big Apple, Senator Warnock also appeared on MSNBC's _Morning Joe_ and CNN's _Anderson Cooper 360_. If you're asking why our opponent skipped a vote on health care for veterans, it's probably because his publisher gave him a cash advance of $250,000 for the book.

In fact, while Georgians have struggled under the massive inflation caused by the Biden-Warnock agenda, _**Raphael Warnock has more than doubled his income**_ since getting elected to the U.S. Senate.

I've got an important message for Mr. Warnock: **The United States Senate isn't a part-time job, and the people's seat should not be used to enrich yourself.** Veterans who sacrificed for our country deserve better.

Peter,

When my colleagues see me coming, they joke and say, [**"there’s Barr, so it must be something about horses, bourbon, Toyota, coal, or the University of Kentucky!"**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=773f73583037408eace332926b3b1221&_e=4dHTNFsPVlXa-WrX5cvR0CvgydTV8JptsYD6sD7VT4PAAsuHx-v-LwXO0KJgNCCtrCqcLeic_UvVgRIMkNrNmucbrMeU0i-cEMx6OgiWNToa4xOvA4Bd51kwna9uhXvgG5NA3ywOL-JvrZlm3uWc5ijs-oIJ3dRzOuo0UO3CE1V9Se5A-eIhWDQir0b4WypYVwFBfdhlKz8OMDtqM0Mu4f8Zzmo4b_WHfRcRAgoK27EyRiZDYxKYWk5AOPoL1DXyoh3HNDKPmWJ2v9BExF9Hx8kNcovZJAqAILEKBu6roiM_TZa3AFm5P_7aGJk6Jm59akp1hUr_OOnEnu9zoaIEWQjc8xmtDQGUlH6TfhZedAfEKLPhllFnKPQxmLG-gPXn)

_And they’re not wrong..._ I bleed Kentucky through and through. It’s where my family has always been, it’s the place that shaped me into the man I am, and it’s the Commonwealth that I’ve been so blessed to represent in Congress.

Now, towards the end of this email, I’m going to request something from you, but first, I want you to understand who I am, how I became the man I am, and what I’m hoping for my future and the future of my daughters.

Growing up, my sister was diagnosed with juvenile arthritis. Our family had to come together to support her treatment. _This taught me that family is the most important thing, compassion is essential, struggle is inevitable, and perseverance is necessary._

It also showed me the need for high-quality, affordable and accessible healthcare for families - [**which continues to be a top issue for me in Congress.**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=773f73583037408eace332926b3b1221&_e=4dHTNFsPVlXa-WrX5cvR0CvgydTV8JptsYD6sD7VT4PAAsuHx-v-LwXO0KJgNCCtrCqcLeic_UvVgRIMkNrNmucbrMeU0i-cEMx6OgiWNToa4xOvA4Bd51kwna9uhXvgG5NA3ywOL-JvrZlm3uWc5ijs-oIJ3dRzOuo0UO3CE1V9Se5A-eIhWDQir0b4WypYVwFBfdhlKz8OMDtqM0Mu4dKuqy9S_OWQk9TW4MQNUoFVsDKSMpYuzAdLWURK1x29tITmSJhxcGCHRvWjhwt4diuOJ43R8J-RpFxDLjCh_3-NbIgFibK55cd-u3ACDCyOLfIfRq3CopQnHUbvMvPcfVGmTNdqPickUdxSEPq8-F49tLzEYULi1C_P_XETiMlJ)

My love for Kentucky met my interest in politics when I first interned in Washington in college. The ability to work on and fight for legislative policies that helped conservative causes was so rewarding.

body:
One colleague in Congress said they were “shocked” to see how hostile her own party was towards Alexandria from the moment she arrived — and she still faces hostility to this day.
# [](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/143?refcode=em20220914-3391-header&t=1&akid=3391%2E2526796%2EGAhfo8)
Alexandria’s community sent her to Congress on purpose to disrupt and challenge a lot of what’s wrong in D.C.
But during her first term, many people in her own party said her election was a fluke, a mistake, and that there was “nothing to worry about.” Many believed that Alexandria would be a one-term Congresswoman.
One colleague in Congress said they were “shocked” to see how hostile her own party was towards Alexandria from the moment she arrived — and she still faces hostility to this day.
It was clear from the beginning that the party never wanted Alexandria there. It’s why a Moderate Democrat mounted a $3 million primary challenge and why Republicans spent over $10 million trying to unseat her in 2020.
**But now Alexandria is facing off with a MAGA Republican opponent in the general election this November.** They’ve already set up a massive #OustAOC sign in Queens, so we need to be ready to fight back against their posters, mailers, commercials, and whatever else they’ll throw at us in these last 8 weeks.
[Can we count on your first $3 contribution today to help us fight back against their disinformation about our Congresswoman with deep organizing and truth telling?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-202209-so.z544IY&refcode=em20220914-3391-P_FND_EGR_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=3391%2E2526796%2EGAhfo8)

But during her first term, many people in her own party said her election was a fluke, a mistake, and that there was “nothing to worry about.” Many believed that Alexandria would be a one-term Congresswoman. One colleague in Congress said they were “shocked” to see how hostile her own party was towards Alexandria from the moment she arrived — and she still faces hostility to this day. It was clear from the beginning that the party never wanted Alexandria there. It’s why a Moderate Democrat mounted a $3 million primary challenge and why Republicans spent over $10 million trying to unseat her in 2020. But now Alexandria is facing off with a MAGA Republican opponent in the general election this November. They’ve already set up a massive #OustAOC sign in Queens, so we need to be ready to fight back against their posters, mailers, commercials, and whatever else they’ll throw at us in these last 8 weeks. We need to show the widespread support for Alexandria to send her back to Congress so she can continue doing what she was elected to do: demand better. Every dollar, no matter the amount, shows the widespread support for our priorities from NY-14 and beyond. Our sincerest thanks, Team AOC | ---|--- | | ---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

Peter, I want you to hear the harsh truth from me, Peter.

**Virginia is one of the most expensive media markets in the country.**

That means it’s _extra expensive_ to get our ads on the air, and at the rate we’re fundraising now, we’re going to have to make some tough choices about the future of our campaign.

**If we’re going to have the resources we need to run our ads in Virginia, we need a MAJOR fundraising push from our grassroots donors.**

There is no one better to represent the people of Florida _(and no one better to tell you why than me!)_ 😊

My wife is the first openly queer Black woman to be elected in Florida at _any level._ They understand the toll that discriminatory and hateful legislation takes on LGBTQ+ folks _on a personal level._

She has always stood up against Ron DeSantis and his hateful crew, and she will continue to stand up to anyone who suggests, through word or legislation, that we deserve less rights for loving who we love.

Fellow patriot,

With just 55 days until Election Day, I wanted to remind you and conservatives around the country why I'm running for election in the "most competitive House race in Texas."

If you're reading this now, then there is a good chance that you've read the email I'm including below. That said, I really think it's worth reading again given the limited amount of time we have remaining before voters head to the polls.

I've been running for Congress now for nearly three years, so it goes without saying that this race has become my life over the last 36 months. **[I'd be honored if you'd let me remind you why my campaign is worth supporting.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d595541907b4452d81f37dd757dbcbdf&_e=ecuabfMdZfWPFsG5CASm5AlCA2sCUU8tCAoYLAW09MpQHny1dx_d-wuxKkuv9ndPw-gBoGxLYM9F1NBibL3PpYhP4n3yh6vNiADPHFyPLFiumJhROmWr9M8hehPTZ9Rq-_i5wlGLLILiPRUYlo9MnhGZ8r3h9FWek61JTDTsKlmKcwgR9NyjA0m6BoljknSAyGdxQlIvZ-3_KeTbr6_Qp3kpwCdEwPsc9ap5dubAI3yz-JuGQ7zIv46E7LmUWmOcIFf2Id2v0KLMZtWlp5gjz1ikFMjEfd6AO75jIaKFvFbKYtOFHf0acve9977z5q-Wba1XuJW8mDjeqcWn7dUb-zeWtYQfs74aCqDLQ5RlanaItxmqkJ0wxiVBi1bldH_H0glsqYr6CGdJ025DO3CcTviAhxPkiWpVh166XAWgVj0%3D)**

**This Message Originally Appeared in Email Inboxes from May 2021**

Not too long ago, Hispanics were _expected_ and _assumed_ to be Democrats by anyone with a passive interest in political demography. In fact, **until recently, Hispanics were about as Democrat as suburbanites were Republican.**

I’m helping to change that narrative. I’m not a **“coconut”** - - brown on the outside, white on the inside - as some have called me. And I’m certainly not a **“self-hating Hispanic,”** as others have labeled me. My name is Monica De La Cruz, **a proud Hispanic Republican,** and I’m running for Congress in Texas’ 15th Congressional District to flip a seat RED which has never been held by a Republican in its HISTORY.

In 2020, I ran for the same seat in Congress I’m running for today. We ran one heck of a campaign and fell short by **_just_ 6,588 votes.** I didn’t get to the top of the hill in 2020, but I’m a fighter - I never give up. body:
Hog Day, Creedmoor Music Fest, & more! | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/bbae3fd61365/valerie-offers-no-solutions-in-town-hall-last-night-9060925?e=20ac8f046f)
---
| |
Dear Peter, My name is Courtney Geels, and I want to represent you in U.S. Congress. I want to hear what issues are important to YOU so I know how to best represent you when I get there. So let’s talk about them!

I'd love for you to join me this weekend at one of these local events and chat about your concerns.

Join me in Hillsborough at Hog Day, in Creedmoor at the Creedmoor Music Festival, or in Graham at the Kinfolk Concert Series! Scroll below for all the details:
---
|
---
| Enjoy some of the best BBQ in the southeast and meet with Courtney to discuss current events affecting our nation today! In addition, this two day festival provides live music, handcrafted gifts, emergency vehicle display, and much more! Funds raised from this event go to support youth programs and services.
---
| [Learn More About Hog Day](https://courtneygeelsforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0ca724a68d4210b231de53e89&id=de6e2167ab&e=20ac8f046f "Learn More About Hog Day")
---
|
---
| Join Courtney at the 29th annual Creedmoor Music Festival. Enjoy local vendors and music while taking the time to meet and speak with Courtney on various topics moving our nation today. There will be two tables set up. Check out the GOP table to learn more about the candidates, then stop by the Candidates table to meet Courtney!
---
| [Learn More About the Creedmoor Music Festival](https://courtneygeelsforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0ca724a68d4210b231de53e89&id=96b365fef4&e=20ac8f046f "Learn More About the Creedmoor Music Festival")
---
|
---
| Featuring Buttermilk Creek Bluegrass & The Mason Lovette Band, this event honors all Medical Healthcare professionals, Fire, Police, Sheriff, and Emergency Management personnel. It is also to honor the families of these individuals who have tirelessly and selflessly supported them while they supported our community during the Covid crisis. Join us as we support the cause!
---
| [Learn More about the Our Community Heroes Concert](https://courtneygeelsforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0ca724a68d4210b231de53e89&id=8f9e0dbfed&e=20ac8f046f "Learn More about the Our Community Heroes Concert")
---
| I can't wait to meet you this weekend!

For truth, justice, and unity,

_Courtney_

body:
This email is a bit longer than normal, so I hope you’ll read the whole thing. This email is a bit longer than normal, so I hope you’ll read the whole thing. |
_No longer want to receive emails from Andy Barr for Congress? You may [unsubscribe dpwillis67@gmail.com here](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/e/encryptedUnsubscribe?_r=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_s=90dfea648c40452cb486d3f37fd417b0&_t=NFhkAuPWxGZB7g4LXAhkFLTZoJ64yIPHvJDo9nEeyFxBL30WyIJkmg-jIIrS2XtAGkgRDooCVlc9hL0MnPLb7Ed53_2H9SzvsEP3RI5EMlw%3D)._

[](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=90dfea648c40452cb486d3f37fd417b0&_e=VO47Uj5bJCIu-EdrHMVzpEPwa0cxs12KXZDqQwuCzfHyfypxcp5WrNZRHKSL-0OtLUNqw-NOk5Q3XdWmrYVrYuLth1TN410uaLtujnsyn3k6IyH-8EVj1gNrZBSSB9lNqSmtfjnC4SbHgAoPN_CFmqpisvBJIG2x1QBZihxortcS2Omq_JiVWyzDPwafUnue-dJ9nUfIpVzXceQzz0c4cW9cyp_dOTA2qz5ftiu44M4ss_SHl9U14iU09WCK9gxR_X7cp-MmMb8GG5FUgBluIhGB_U2w4Qb5UQIJ05CSI8WO_6PIFDTU4YzYFouepwmcCQXcJbsfdqRY3NTp0a-2XoJzBb3yX5h7WDy6Fk5eepeK8LyfN67CTl45MzkPS9yv)

---
Peter,

When my colleagues see me coming, they joke and say, [**"there’s Barr, so it must be something about horses, bourbon, Toyota, coal, or the University of Kentucky!"**](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=90dfea648c40452cb486d3f37fd417b0&_e=VO47Uj5bJCIu-EdrHMVzpEPwa0cxs12KXZDqQwuCzfHyfypxcp5WrNZRHKSL-0OtLUNqw-NOk5Q3XdWmrYVrYuLth1TN410uaLtujnsyn3k6IyH-8EVj1gNrZBSSB9lNqSmtfjnC4SbHgAoPN_CFmqpisvBJIG2x1QBZihxortcS2Omq_JiVWyzDPwafUnue-dJ9nUfIpVzXceQzz0c4cajd8eXSwtM-eG1xT-HER2Ui-ns_nyFIyNtJT51IhLOfL926cJDjPImy2H5NV5vjrOg1d2j0nCO5zhEmnzCw0cG-lmt1cm2c6O_EQHCxBG1e-FuthV-2g40wbbd09pvG6Gf6q4Vtx963fPMoSkCG3w3ofXbHN3wkkdQ_n5dB7gpK)

_And they’re not wrong..._ I bleed Kentucky through and through. It’s where my family has always been, it’s the place that shaped me into the man I am, and it’s the Commonwealth that I’ve been so blessed to represent in Congress.

Now, towards the end of this email, I’m going to request something from you, but first, I want you to understand who I am, how I became the man I am, and what I’m hoping for my future and the future of my daughters.

Growing up, my sister was diagnosed with juvenile arthritis. Our family had to come together to support her treatment. _This taught me that family is the most important thing, compassion is essential, struggle is inevitable, and perseverance is necessary._

It also showed me the need for high-quality, affordable and accessible healthcare for families - [**which continues to be a top issue for me in Congress.**](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=90dfea648c40452cb486d3f37fd417b0&_e=VO47Uj5bJCIu-EdrHMVzpEPwa0cxs12KXZDqQwuCzfHyfypxcp5WrNZRHKSL-0OtLUNqw-NOk5Q3XdWmrYVrYuLth1TN410uaLtujnsyn3k6IyH-8EVj1gNrZBSSB9lNqSmtfjnC4SbHgAoPN_CFmqpisvBJIG2x1QBZihxortcS2Omq_JiVWyzDPwafUnue-dJ9nUfIpVzXceQzz0c4cW9cyp_dOTA2qz5ftiu44M44motFn2OdKxZBzVxMAPPD5KYaR9h_pOnMtdd3Sb5H5fOLanA_PBOs0YdXfW2-elDvWnrdjdwB10tM_62p30CesVmzIa_M1bG-3hTGEKQPPSmkABOesC6I5faDVFr7XXqoY8nAJZe0pfg668J9Cl7w)

My love for Kentucky met my interest in politics when I first interned in Washington in college. The ability to work on and fight for legislative policies that helped conservative causes was so rewarding.

Ultimately, I took a chance and ran for Congress in my hometown of Lexington against an incumbent Democrat and lost by 647 votes in one of the closest races in the country. But I recalled the lessons I learned as a child, and I persevered. Two years later I ran again and I was elected. Team,
We’ve said it before and we’ll say it again: Elissa is running in one of the most competitive seats in the country. And major news outlets agree. Both USA Today and Roll Call recently released lists of the most vulnerable House seats, and Elissa was included on both.
Something that’s particularly concerning? There are 7 Democratic incumbents on the USA Today list and 6 on the Roll Call list — and Republicans only need 5 seats to retake the House. You can read the full analysis from USA Today ( here [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2022/09/03/house-of-representatives-midterm-election-races-to-watch-updates/7894769001/] ) and Roll Call ( here [https://rollcall.com/2022/09/13/after-primaries-these-10-house-members-are-most-vulnerable/] ).
But, not only is this one of the most competitive, we just got word from AdImpact, an advertisement tracking agency, that it’s also the most *expensive* House race in the country. A whopping $20 million (!!!) has been spent or reserved on television so far.
We know what you’re wondering: how do you win in one of the most competitive AND the most expensive House races in the entire country? The answer is with grassroots support.
The vast majority of the money in this race is being spent on advertising by super PACs (groups that can raise and spend an unlimited amount of money to support any candidate they would like). There are a couple of big differences between the money super PACs spend vs candidates themselves. Namely, in the 60 days before an election, TV stations must give candidates a lower rate to air their own ads and communicate with voters.
We just entered that 60 day window, so the price of advertisements has dropped quite a bit. That means we’re able to make our money go quite a bit further than the super PACs are – and in such an expensive election that’s everything.
So, here’s our ask: will you send a few dollars our way to help us as we: fight back against the super PACs, help Democrats keep the majority, and compete in the one of the most competitive and expensive House races in the country? | | | | | Peter, **Lauren Boebert wants us all to die.** No, you didn't read that wrong...In fact, there isn't much that hasn't been said about Lauren Boebert at this point. Friend,

Because he's the cosponsor of a "fetal personhood" bill that would classify ALL abortions as murder at conception. body:
Ducey joins Mitch McConnell and Donald Trump in a legacy of judicial appointments | |
---
| | |
---
| | | Hello,

When you think of Republicans who have prioritized judicial appointments, you think of Mitch McConnell and Donald Trump.

But a recent op-ed in Real Clear Policy points out that Gov. Doug Ducey has set the example for what a Republican governor can do to ensure a quality, conservative judiciary.
---
|
---
|
## [This Governor Should Set the Republican Example on Courts](https://dougducey.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bf4fbf102e325035a83ef3427&id=8fcc8f4091&e=55d4e2f84a)

By [Glenn Hamer](https://dougducey.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bf4fbf102e325035a83ef3427&id=1457c3b32e&e=55d4e2f84a)
September 14, 2022

When you think of Republican officeholders who understand the importance of judges and policy, the first names that pop to mind are Mitch McConnell and Donald Trump. They indeed put great effort into populating the bench with conservatives.

But Gov. Doug Ducey of Arizona was implementing a comprehensive judicial strategy before the Trump-McConnell duo worked their magic. Given the potential of judges to make mischief with their decisions, Republican governors across the country would do well to emulate what Ducey has done over eight years.

For years, the Arizona judiciary was a mish-mash. No governor put much energy into identifying judges with a coherent judicial philosophy. By the time Gov. Ducey took office, this had resulted in a State Supreme Court with a decidedly liberal bent.

Ducey’s first step was to expand the state Supreme Court from five members to seven. The move had been anticipated by many – the court building was constructed to accommodate seven justices – and yet when the legislature approved the expansion there was a hue and cry, led by the usual suspects on the left, who claimed it was unnecessary. The real reason is that the Supreme Court served as a potential blockade for conservative, free market policies passed at the legislature, and a protector of liberal ideas advanced by out-of-state special interests in the form of ballot initiatives.

The business community understood this reality. The Arizona Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which I served as president & CEO at the time, strongly supported the expansion of the Court. We stated: “By increasing access to civil justice, systemic efficiency, and the breadth of legal questions the Supreme Court has the opportunity to address, this important piece of legislation would allow the Court to better serve Arizona’s citizens and business community.”

Ducey’s second step was to ensure the Commission on Appellate Court Appointments was filled with people who believe in the rule of law, and feel that judges should not be legislators. The commission is Arizona’s “Missouri model” for selecting judges that makes recommendations to the governor about judicial appointments. Historically, this commission has played games by limiting the recommendations made to the governor, allowing them to tip the scale and infringe on the governor’s authority. No more. This changing of the guard on the commission was a crucial step in ensuring the governor had a steady stream of conservative choices.

Third was the actual appointments. Ducey sent a strong message with his first appointment to the Supreme Court – noted school choice advocate Clint Bolick, who had been a litigator at the Phoenix-based Goldwater Institute. Bolick’s selection was unconventional and a signal that Ducey was willing to consider people who previously would not have been selected. It set the tone for the rest of his appointments.

Ducey’s preparation for interviews with prospective judges was intense. He asked challenging questions to ensure that people shared his philosophy that judges should interpret the law and not legislate from the bench. Asked early in his tenure what surprised him most about being governor, Ducey said, “The amount of time I’m spending on judges. I didn’t expect it, but I’ve come to realize how important it is.”

Arizona has 171 merit selected superior court judges, 19 appeals court judges, and seven Supreme Court judges. By the end of his term, Ducey will have appointed 108 merit selected judges, more than 60% of merit selected judges in Arizona. And now that they’re in place, this year’s state budget gave a substantial pay increase to judges as incentive to stay on the bench instead of leaving for the private sector.

The kicker in all this is the diversity of Ducey’s judicial appointments, with record numbers of women appointed to the bench, minorities to the appellate courts and judges registered to political parties other than his own – something not even Governor Napolitano achieved. Currently almost 40% of his appointments are women – a record for any governor in state history – and his appellate court appointments have included five Hispanics, including the first two Hispanics ever on the Supreme court, the first Asian-Pacific Islander on the Court of Appeals and a judge that identifies as bi-racial. The Arizona judiciary is not an all-white-males club.

Nowhere has the influence of conservative justices been felt more than the all-important area of Ballot Measures. Given conservative dominance of the governor’s office and the legislature, ballot measures have become the preferred method for liberals to pass left-wing policy. For several election cycles now, out-of-state special interests – unions, tax increasers, environmentalists, so-called “election reform” advocates – have dumped tens of millions of dollars into the state to qualify liberal propositions for the ballot.

Historically the courts took a hands-off approach to ballot measures. Anyone who submitted a few hundred thousand signatures was virtually guaranteed to qualify for the ballot. It was so easy for courts to kick the can and just say “let the voters decide,” no matter how egregious the language or the process for submitting signatures was.

Whereas Arizona truly was the Wild West, with its “anything goes” attitude on ballot measures, now the judiciary actually applies the law. The guard rails the legislature has put up to reduce fraud and ensure integrity in the initiative process are actually being enforced. The latest abomination to be kicked off the ballot – a grab bag of liberal policies masquerading as “election reform” – spares Arizona the potential ignominy of having some of the worst election laws in the country. Marc Elias will have to do his work elsewhere in 2022.

Ducey leaves office in January 2023, but one of his most lasting legacies will be the re-shaping of Arizona’s third branch of government. It’s gotten very little attention except for occasional howling from liberal critics, but in terms of ensuring good governance for years to come, and a stable, welcoming environment for job creators, it may be his most lasting achievement. Given the importance of the policy at the state level, other conservative governors would be wise to follow his example, in the process, providing a larger slate of quality judges for future Republican Presidents to appoint to federal and Supreme Court vacancies.

Glenn Hamer is president & CEO of the Texas Association of Business. He ran the Arizona Chamber of Commerce and Industry from 2006-2021.

Given conservative dominance of the governor’s office and the legislature, ballot measures have become the preferred method for liberals to pass left-wing policy. For several election cycles now, out-of-state special interests – unions, tax increasers, environmentalists, so-called “election reform” advocates – have dumped tens of millions of dollars into the state to qualify liberal propositions for the ballot. Historically the courts took a hands-off approach to ballot measures. Anyone who submitted a few hundred thousand signatures was virtually guaranteed to qualify for the ballot. It was so easy for courts to kick the can and just say “let the voters decide,” no matter how egregious the language or the process for submitting signatures was. Whereas Arizona truly was the Wild West, with its “anything goes” attitude on ballot measures, now the judiciary actually applies the law. The guard rails the legislature has put up to reduce fraud and ensure integrity in the initiative process are actually being enforced. The latest abomination to be kicked off the ballot – a grab bag of liberal policies masquerading as “election reform” – spares Arizona the potential ignominy of having some of the worst election laws in the country. Marc Elias will have to do his work elsewhere in 2022. Ducey leaves office in January 2023, but one of his most lasting legacies will be the re-shaping of Arizona’s third branch of government. It’s gotten very little attention except for occasional howling from liberal critics, but in terms of ensuring good governance for years to come, and a stable, welcoming environment for job creators, it may be his most lasting achievement. Given the importance of the policy at the state level, other conservative governors would be wise to follow his example, in the process, providing a larger slate of quality judges for future Republican Presidents to appoint to federal and Supreme Court vacancies. body:
We’re a campaign that can organize and speak to the hopes and needs of voters from the mountains to the coast, rural and urban alike.
#

Sorry to reach out again to ask for your support, but Cheri really needs your help today. But before we ask, will you please give us 90 seconds to explain why your $3 is so important?
We are running the kind of campaign that it takes to flip a Senate seat. It’s a campaign that can organize and speak to the hopes and needs of voters from the mountains to the coast, rural and urban alike.
And so far, it’s working. Despite super PACs swooping in with millions of dollars worth of attack ads since Cheri became our nominee, the polls show us neck and neck with our opponent.
But it takes an enormous amount of resources to run this kind of campaign in a state as large and diverse as North Carolina. Every dollar donated, every voter registered, and every door knocked will matter when the votes are counted.
Honestly, we wish the money that we already raised would be enough, but with the data showing this will be one of the closest races in the entire country, it means it’s also going to be one of the most expensive.
Unlike our opponent, Cheri’s not taking a dime of corporate PAC money, and we’re not banking on super PACs buying this seat either. Instead, we are counting on people like you to power this fight. So please:

Fellow American,

One evening earlier this summer, while the Senate was voting on a veterans' health care bill, Raphael Warnock was nowhere to be found.

He wasn't even in Washington. **He was in New York City filming a segment on _The Late Show with Stephen Colbert_ to promote his new book. **

[](http://links.ourbestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=80ebb41732384ac087921d8b617f32bf&_m=48f02bfea05d4759abb0e206f82c63df&_e=iPyJMiQMKN-fs4xGYHRlqZa-vLwXF_guMwQCWp13ru-7sbuQ-8VDFITmOX4MRM9Gzetcfv3KqS2rF0uSkvfihPQ-hPctBbLfNSqxrV1dLXouFZLHpqWAdCHUMI5h5v51aT7uUwB5FITee6NWYhLdBKKBT4xUlKNtzPemJ53jEtHoneBWYzniJ8BODw1ASpg4suPsVMiZmqXCRt79rjRDVSSs-odJU_eRoOKGCWkI9cPrz8y3vYbRJnBuelt4P1qiV-JCqLMy86H63jgiO9a2munQ5eaGm2qaTZEo7szrLg3MwqJJCSpgVL8Q96bpXTeW_aWWeeapFKaBUOFKXbVkcEYVqwARkcEbTIHkK8_gSmkKnHJMfp5vEKXwwdQz6uA7J1ivcSnoojDasIrr0Zuv4xsbBi1_CALxtMEtvNc0rT4%3D)
Just eighteen months into the job, Senator Warnock is already sending clear signals to Georgians - **particularly veterans** - that selling books is a higher priority than voting on health care benefits for burn pit victims.

_**That's just shameful.**_

During his trip to the Big Apple, Senator Warnock also appeared on MSNBC's _Morning Joe_ and CNN's _Anderson Cooper 360_. If you're asking why our opponent skipped a vote on health care for veterans, it's probably because his publisher gave him a cash advance of $250,000 for the book.

In fact, while Georgians have struggled under the massive inflation caused by the Biden-Warnock agenda, _**Raphael Warnock has more than doubled his income**_ since getting elected to the U.S. Senate.

I've got an important message for Mr. Warnock: **The United States Senate isn't a part-time job, and the people's seat should not be used to enrich yourself.** Veterans who sacrificed for our country deserve better.

I trust you are as infuriated by this behavior as I am.
